findings.text: Without risk control, DeepSeek-R1 jailbreak Unsafe jumps from 25.2% to 85.9%; with risk control jailbreak Unsafe falls to 4.3% while rejection rises to 87.3%.
R1 is weak on [HarmBench](/evals/harmbench) intellectual-property prompts such as lyric generation, which lowers its HarmBench score versus other frontier models.

findings.text: Showing the chain-of-thought lowers [HarmBench](/evals/harmbench) Safety Score (89.3 with risk control, 35.0 without) versus hide-cot (96.3 / 58.0).
On the in-house taxonomy, authors place R1 with risk control in a second safety tier (~10% Unsafe); without risk control they call it relatively unsafe (>20%).

notes: Nature main PDF is 12 pages (printed 633–638 plus Methods/Extended Data); safety numbers are in Supplementary Information section 4.3 (SI pages ~35–46). SI text layer was appended to $W/text.txt for quote checks. Skipped general capability tables (AIME, MATH, LiveCodeBench, Arena-Hard, MMLU, SimpleQA, coding, etc.). Skipped per-language bars in Supplementary Fig. 12 (broken OCR); kept aggregate scores stated in prose. Table 8 Origin Unsafe/Reject duplicates Table 7 Overall, so only Jailbreak and GAP columns were kept. HELM supplied some Table 6 scores but is a leaderboard, so testers is empty. Distill models appear only in capability sections and were left out of covers. No formal risk-framework thresholds; riskDecisions empty. Topics cyber/bio_chem/manipulation/hallucination left uncovered (taxonomy mentions or SimpleQA capability only). Safety results are in the Supplementary Information section 4.3, which is its own document (deepseek-r1-safety); they are not repeated here.
